# Unit 3 reliability — Teacher guide
Draft 14 October 2026. Four explicit lessons across weeks 8–9, two each; existing project workshops and week 10 completion remain allocated. No new weighting or additional assessment.

## Test and lab answers
Fresh Equipment total 2: lend 2 succeeds/available 0; quantity 3 well-formed but excessive =>False/unchanged. Quantity 0/negative/text/bool =>ValueError at model boundary. Unknown IDs and historical duplicate reject without stock/history change. Component suite uses real cooperating objects, so includes integration checks; user acceptance needs the console/user task.
The twelve-test suite test_booking_reliability.py targets the supplied project reference. Run python test_booking_reliability.py -v beside the included support/reference modules. It covers fixture/search/issue, invalid/excess/unknown/duplicate input, complete/repeated return, report/history order, value snapshots, polymorphic queries and normalised IDs. Students adapt interfaces and design further independent cases; passing samples are not proof of fault absence.
fault_return_lab.py is intentionally defective and separate from the reference. python fault_probe.py -v initially reports two failures: repeat returns True, and availability rises to 4 after first return restored 3. Repair with an inactive guard before stock change. fault_return_lab_fixed.py is the separate illustrative teacher repair. Keeping the same two probes after repair supplies regression evidence. A parse failure is syntax; division/index exceptions are runtime; repeated-return overstock is logic.

## Workload answers and limitations
Harness uses sequential synthetic issue history in descending ID order, returns every fourth item, rejects one historical duplicate, performs known/missing searches and repeats active reports. For 100 records: returns 25/active 75; for 1000: returns 250/active 750. For 1: returns 1/active 0. Correctness, stock and history order are checked alongside timing. Optional CSV writes/reads a new synthetic file, reports byte count and separate durations; existing files are not overwritten. This is not live deployment, concurrency capacity, persistent project reload or a universal threshold. Set real criteria/environment before a pass/fail performance decision.
Report worst time O(h+m²), extra report space O(m), where h is retained history and m active records. Insertion sorting costs depend on order; repeated elapsed timings depend on environment and measured boundaries. Batch issue/mixed timings include their loop and checks; report correctness checks occur outside each timed report call. Median/max refer only to measured report repeats. Start with the bounded small classroom runs; harness range 1–5000/repeats 1–10 is a tool contract, not a business capacity requirement.

## Review/responsibility evidence
Useful review names trigger, requirement, state fault and a focused correction plus affected regressions. Version comparison and recoverable backup serve related but different purposes; restoration must be demonstrated. Acknowledge source/authorship and check permission/licence conditions, respond to quality feedback, disclose session-loss limits, protect user records and verify unsupported claims. Discuss malware provenance, reliance, social sharing/cyber safety, information quality and developer rights/responsibilities through the original cases. Do not run unknown software or use real borrower data in these activities.
Teacher solutions remain separate, not access-protected. This pack is a classroom draft and samples relevant testing/maintenance/responsibility content; it does not declare complete Unit 3 coverage.

Additional responses: tiny text/colour-only feedback requires ergonomic and inclusive interface choices with explicit feedback and user trials. Document assistance, follow the relevant code of conduct, neither create nor transmit malware, and recognise developers’ own contributions as well as those of others.
